Commentary.Commentary: Right then! India Women players stride out to the middle. Alyssa Healy and Beth Mooney are the openers for Australia Women. Jhulan Goswami to start with the ball.

Mithali Raj has given the signal for declaration as Jhulan Goswami and Meghna Singh are running off. India Women have declared on 377/8. India started Day 3 with a score of 276/5 on the board. Taniya Bhatia and Deepti Sharma were off to a decent start as they kept on piling up runs on the board by rotating the strike at regular intervals. The latter brought her second Test fifty too. Pooja Vastrakar hung around the middle for a while but fell right before the Dinner to Ellyse Perry which was also her 300th wicket in all formats. After the break, Stella Campbell scalped Deepti Sharma who was looking in good touch. Now, India Women have 377 runs on the board and have asked Australia Women to come out and bat in the twilight period. It will be interesting to see how the Aussies reply to the India Women bowlers in this twilight period as the pink ball is expected to move more.

...Session 2...

India Women are ahead in the game and are clearly dictating terms at the moment. They are running away with the game. Australia Women, on the other hand, would look to come back and chip wickets at regular intervals to make inroads in the game. Do join us at 1710 local (0710 GMT) for the second session.

Australia Women remain on the hunt! The bowlers probed good lines and lengths but could not find much success. They surely made it hard for the batters to score run. Stella Campbell was really good with the ball. She troubled the batters with her variations and got the breakthrough of the day, which was also her first wicket in Test cricket. At the very end, Perry came back into the attack to get the better of Pooja Vastrakar. Although, it was not a good day in the field for them. They dropped a couple of catches, only if these were taken the story would’ve been completely different.

Good work with the blade continues for India! Taniya Bhatia and Deepti Sharma picked up things from where they left off on Day 2. Both the batters were looking solid in the middle, albeit, they were not allowed to score freely. Taniya Bhatia ould not stick around throughout the session and was skittled out at 22 runs. Later, Pooja Vastrakar and Deepti Sharma continued the good work, while the latter went on to grab her second half century in Tests. But India lost Pooja Vastrakar at the very end of the session. Not the end they were looking for.

It was a good first session on Day 3. India Women would be the happier side going into the break. Australia Women did not trouble the batters much, as they could not pick wickets at regular intervals. But they did take a late wicket, before heading into Dinner. Will this help get a shift in the momentum?

OUT! TAKEN! Ellyse Perry picks up her 300th wicket in all formats. But this wicket belongs to Beth Mooney. Perry delivers a length ball, outside off. Pooja Vastrakar is tempted to play the cover drive and goes after it. The ball kisses the outside edge and flies towards the second slip where Beth Mooney dives to her left and takes the catch. An excellent catch from her. Pooja Vastrakar has to walk back to the pavilion. THAT WILL BE DINNER ON DAY 3.

The spirit of the game is still alive, thanks to Punam Raut! She did the unexpected. Raut got caught behind, but the umpire did not raise his finger. Even though after seeing that, Raut decided to walk off the pitch. She knew she had got the slightest of edge on that one, but in the age of DRS, we will hardly see any player walk off without getting any confirmation. The Indian camp was in a shock after seeing that at first, but Raut certainly earned respect to keep the game fair.

PITCH REPORT - The wicket looks still great after two days of cricket and there is even coverage of grass. There are blue skies and sunshine out in the middle. It should be an even contest between bat and ball.

Hello and a very warm welcome Day 3 of this one-off day and night Test match between Australia Women and India Women. Just like day 1, the second day was also incomplete due to severe weather conditions. This now means that we've got a little over two days of play left to get a result and we are still in the first innings. Let's talk about the action on day 2, Smriti Mandhana notched up a beautiful century but the Aussies did make inroads as well. India Women though, finished with 276/5 on the board and are still a bit ahead in the game. For Australia Women to have any chance of winning this game, they need to get rid of the Indian tailenders soon and then bat out of their skins as well. The forecast for the day seems good and hopefully we should get a full day's play in today. India Women are in command but this one looks to be heading towards a draw. Can either team step on the gas and take the bull by the horns? Find out soon.

The game though seems to be heading towards a draw! Difficult to see a result being squeezed out with! On Day 3 though, India will somehow look to cross the 350-run mark. There is not a lot of batting to come and a lot will depend on the pair batting currently if they are to do so. Australia, on the other hand, were a lot better with the ball on Friday and they would want to repeat that performance, take the remaining wickets quickly and then bat well. Do join us for all the action at 2 pm local (4 am GMT). Cheers and take care.

Update 8.48 pm local (10.48 am GMT) - So, once again it is rain who has played the spoilsport as play has been suspended for the day! We had under 50 overs on Day 1 and we have had just over 50 on Day 2. Have to say, one can't really say which team would have ended on top but Australia will be happy with how they managed to crawl back into the game. The day though was begun well by the Indians as Mandhana first got to her ton. She along with Raut also got the 100-run stand up. Australia though then got both the batters in quick succession. The visitors then looked to up the ante after Dinner but they once again lost wickets on a regular basis which got Australia right back into the game.

Update 8.09 pm local (10.09 am GMT) - The wait continues! The conditions haven't improved. There is still lightning around in the area and the ground will take time to dry out. The umpires will have a look at 8.30 pm local.

Update 7.34 pm local (9.34 am GMT) - We are not going to have a timely start after Tea as it is still raining and the ground has taken a beating. The ground does drain quickly but it will be a tough task for the groundsmen. There has not been an inspection yet. All we can do is hope that we get some play as soon as possible. Stay with us.

Update 7.11 pm local (9.11 am GMT) - So, the umpires then have decided to take Tea! Just around 18 overs in this session but entertaining 18 overs. Both Raj and Bhatia came out with intent after the break, runs started to come at a decent click for India but both fell in quick succession. At one stage India looked on course to probably post something around 400 but with only the all-rounders left, Australia have a chance to keep them under 350 but for that, they will have to bowl well. Can they do that? We will find out if the weather does clear up and we get some play after the break.

Update 6.46 pm local (8.46 am GMT) - Apparently, the rainstorm has just turned into a hailstorm. It looks bleak currently and it looks like we are in for a long delay. Let's hope that it gets better soon. Stay with us.

Update 6.24 pm (8.24 am GMT) - Well, the umpires are asking the players to go off the field as there is lightning in the area and the covers are coming on as well. It is not raining currently but there is some forecast. Let's hope that we get back on the field as soon as possible. For now though, the safety of the players is of the utmost importance. The rain has also started to come down now. Not heavy but enough to keep the players off the field. Stay tuned.

Australia will look to build on this after the break. They have taken the second new ball and have two relatively new batters out there. The ball might just do a little bit more after the break but can they capitalise? India, on the other hand, will look to play out the second new cherry unscathed and then try to score quickly. The second session is an important one, do join us for it at 5.10 pm local (7.10 am GMT).

On that note, hello and a warm welcome to the second day's play between Australia Women and India Women.

India on the other hand, will try and do that. However, the forecast for Friday is not promising too, let us hope though we do get a full day's of play. The play from Day 2 will begin 30 minutes early to make up for lost time on Day 1. The action will begin at 2 pm local (4 am GMT). Do join us then. Cheers and take care.

The visitors will be a little disappointed that they could have only 44 overs of play, especially Mandhana who was in some form. Right from the word go, she was timing the ball beautifully, scoring boundaries at will. The left-handed opener has more than half the runs of India on Day 1 and is the sole reason why India head into Day 2 in such a strong position.
